qs.q: A 65-year-old female with a 30 pack-year smoking history presents with progressive exertional dyspnea and clubbing. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates a reduced total lung capacity with a normal or increased FEV1/FVC ratio. Which pathophysiological feature characterizes this condition?
o: Increased compliance of lung parenchyma from destruction.
Chronic mucus hypersecretion causing airway obstruction.
Airway hyperresponsiveness triggered by allergen exposure.
Permanent dilatation of respiratory bronchioles with air.
Restricted expansion of lung tissue due to fibrosis.
qs.e: Restrictive pulmonary diseases feature reduced lung volumes, decreased compliance, and increased work of breathing.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: Internal Medicine Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A 68-year-old woman presents with progressive shortness of breath and a non-productive cough over the past year. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates a reduced total lung capacity (54% of predicted) and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 84%. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
qs.e: A reduced total lung capacity accompanied by a normal or increased FEV1/FVC ratio indicates a restrictive lung process such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Obstructive lung diseases such as COPD present with a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio.
qs.s: Introduction to Pulmonary Pathology and Atelectasis: MCQs
